_doc: What hunts the men, and how a shot lands (docs/threats.md; src/smyana/threats.lobster). Times in seconds, distances in tiles. hit: a ball hits 'near' in a hundred at 'near_tiles' or closer, falling to 'far' at the rifle's full range; the target's cover (0..100) takes off up to 'cover_halves' hundredths of that. A hit takes 'wound' hp (a man has 40: the first hit wounds him, the second kills him), or all of it at 'kill_tiles' or closer. 'wounded_pace': how fast a wounded man walks, in hundredths. hearing: how far a shot is heard, by the kind of place (data/guns.json's places). seen_after_shot_s: a man who fired is seen through his cover this long after (the smoke hangs over him). keep_s: a rifleman keeps on the one he is firing at this long after losing sight of him. men_sight: how far the men see, as the patrol's sight.

patrol._doc: The Ottoman patrol (#62): zaptiye in fezzes and turbans with long flintlocks. sight: tiles on a clear day in the open (cover, night and weather cut it: route.lobster's spots). lose_s: no man seen this long, and they search the last place for search_s, then go back to their road. break_share: when fewer than this share (in a hundred) are left, they fall back the way they came. heard_spread: how far off a shot's place they guess it, tiles. The unit is the men's rifle with another slot; looks are data/voxel/bodies/patrol_NN.json; sash: their colour where the men wear red.

wolves._doc: The wolves of the deep fir woods (#60). They follow the men at follow_tiles (winter's, bold, closer at follow_bold_tiles), are heard more than seen, and scatter scatter_tiles away from any shot they hear for scatter_s. At night winter's wolves rush a man who is more than alone_tiles from the next man, if one of them is within sight tiles of him (by smell: cover doesn't hide him), and draw off if he gets back within rejoined_tiles of the others. flee_after: this many down and the pack is gone. howl_s: how often one howls while they follow, at least and at most. The unit bites (melee): 10 a bite, a bite a second and a half.
